page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n4 server family. It is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel x86_64 cores with hyperthreading enabled. The instance provides 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The underlying Intel processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and tile operations, Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations place the n4-standard-16 consistently in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. In single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, the instance achieved scores of 1658.38 and 13633.06 respectively. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1107.55 GB/sec, which drops to 117.6 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 67.32 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates strong performance in specific areas, notably in Geekbench text processing with a score of 2423.0 and small-model LLM text generation at 282.68 tokens/sec, both ranking in the top 25% tier. Other workloads, such as static web serving at 22.14 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 17.13 million operations per second, align with mid-range expectations.

From a resource density perspective, the n4-standard-16 offers a balanced hardware profile that avoids the premium costs associated with specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The absence of local storage and integrated GPUs makes it a cost-efficient choice for workloads reliant on network-attached storage and standard CPU execution. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and solid multi-threaded decompression capabilities, this instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads. These include software compilation, web serving, database operations, and moderate text processing or light machine learning inference tasks.
